ai.description: This slender snake reaches 50 cm. It is dark brown with thin, white crossbars and a white labial region. A distinctive feature is the lack of a loreal scale and smooth, glossy dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Barred Wolf Snake is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, white, Y-shaped or chevron-shaped mark on the nape of its neck, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Barred Wolf Snake inhabits dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and rocky outcrops across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Barred Wolf Snake is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt geckos and skinks by prowling through rock crevices and leaf litter.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon striatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Barred Wolf Snake is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Himalayan foothills to southern India, typically below 1,500 meters.
